name: Drought
value: Sudan record-dry rains; no famine declared
summary: Sudan's rainy season was its driest in over three decades and the IPC warns famine risk is growing; no new declaration
state: Sudan's July–September rains were the lowest nationally in more than three decades, with North Darfur its driest since 1984, and farmers in Gedaref expect a fraction of last year's crop (Reuters via TimesLIVE, 23 Oct). The IPC warned on 12 Oct that famine risk is growing in conflict-affected areas. Sudan is not a major exporter, and searches on 21 Nov found no new famine declaration driven by drought and no harvest failure at a major exporter, so severe drought in crop regions keeps Watch.
for_you: Drought in Sudan, the Horn of Africa and the Sahel mainly affects people there, through hunger and higher local food prices. Global grain supply is not currently disrupted by drought.
rubric_hit: Watch: severe drought in a major crop region (Sudan's driest rainy season in 30+ years); no famine declaration or major exporter failure

sources.title: TimesLIVE (Reuters) — New famine risk haunts war-torn Sudan with El Niño-driven drought
The Star (Reuters) — New famine risk haunts war-torn Sudan with El Niño-driven drought

why: Drought slowly destroys harvests, hydropower and river shipping, and drives famine and migration.
drivers: Rainfall deficits, heat, ENSO, groundwater depletion.

rubric.alert: Drought driving famine conditions, a major exporter's harvest failure, or monsoon failure across a major breadbasket.
rubric.watch: Severe drought in a major crop region, a major river at record low, or a monsoon running more than 20% below normal.
rubric.normal: No major breadbasket in severe drought.
